# Sparse, fixed-design Poisson compilers for local generator errors

16 October 2026. Independent mathematical derivation and small-matrix verification. No canonical source was changed.

## Result and scope

There is a useful escape from the full-patch `2 nu/d²` diamond-ball obstruction, provided the physical error interface supplies a **known sparse Pauli coefficient pattern with coefficient bounds**. It does not require the error itself to be Lindblad.

For traceless Hermitian Pauli strings `P_a`, write the allowed error as

`E(rho) = sum_ab C_ab (P_a rho P_b - {P_b P_a,rho}/2) - i[H,rho]`,

where `C=C†` may be indefinite and `H=sum_p h_p P_p`, with real `h_p`. Suppose, before the error is selected,

`|C_ab| <= M_ab`, `M_ab=M_ba>=0`, and `|h_p|<=u_p`.

There is an explicit fixed, implemented Pauli-dephasing floor `F`, using only original Pauli labels, their pair products at allowed nonzero coefficient positions, and Hamiltonian labels, such that for every allowed error

`F+E = sum_e lambda_e (Phi_e-Id)`,

with every `Phi_e` CPTP, every `lambda_e` independent of the unknown coefficients, and

`sum_e lambda_e <= 2 sum_ab M_ab + 2 sum_p u_p`.                         (R)

The ordered sum `sum_ab` counts each offdiagonal pair twice. Each correlated-pair proposal has at most four Kraus operators and is supported on the union of its two Pauli supports. Thus weight-`k` Pauli noise labels require at most weight-`2k` pair events and product floors. A bounded geometric diameter and bounded incident rate are separate necessary hypotheses: small body count alone does not imply locality.

This is a coefficient-structured robustness neighborhood, not an improved arbitrary diamond-norm ball. The fixed floor must really be present in the generator. Its strength and support, and all proposal rates, are charged. Dense or high-weight expansions of correction-jump errors can destroy the advantage.

The Choi criterion, generalized Schur complement, Lindblad gauge shifts, and Poisson-channel semigroups used below are established machinery. The sparse fixed-design synthesis and its application to the supplied memory construction are derived here; historical priority for this precise packaging has not been established. The known single-Pauli Hamiltonian/dephasing calculation is used only as an ingredient.

    V=P+i sqrt(I-P²).

The commuting positive functions give V†V=I and P=(V+V†)/2. Therefore

    A=(UV+UV†)/2.

The two coefficients have total absolute value1. For a norm-bounded known operator use ||A|| times this construction (zero operators are omitted). This is elementary polar/functional-calculus machinery; no historical novelty is asserted. Finite dimension is important for the unitary polar extension used here.

All dictionary unitaries are fixed before unknown scalar errors are selected. If A=XΠ with a known unitary X and projector Π, take U=X and V=Π+i(I−Π); no dense Pauli expansion or spectral search is needed to state that dictionary. Computing or implementing U,V for general input operators is a separate, potentially dimension-dependent cost. A promise ||unknown delta A||<=epsilon does not supply its polar direction or a fixed dictionary.

16 October 2026. Worker `gd_compiler_genesis`. All assertions below are conditional mathematical statements. The source worktree and supplied originals were read only. Historical priority, external correctness and physical qualification are not established.

## 1. Contract and notation

For a square operator on a finite-dimensional patch, write

\[
\mathcal D[A](\rho)=A\rho A^\dagger-\tfrac12\{A^\dagger A,\rho\}.
\]

A *fixed local compiler* consists of an actually installed Lindblad floor \(F\), and positive proposal rates \(\lambda_e\), selected before the unknown error coefficients are selected. For every allowed error \(E\), the exact equality is

\[
F+E=\sum_e\lambda_e(\Phi_{e,E}-\mathrm{Id}),\qquad \Phi_{e,E}\text{ CPTP}.
\]

The proposal channel may depend on the realized coefficients. The clock rates, floor and support envelope do not. Such channels can be an alternative mathematical unravelling; the apparatus need not synthesize the coefficient-dependent Kraus representation if it implements the generator on the left. Implementing the fixed floor remains a real requirement. An arbitrary unknown operator direction is not inferred from an operator-norm bound.

Two new results are established here:

* A specified finite dictionary of local correction/error operators has a fixed compiler with no Pauli coefficient-conversion factor. For one jump replacement on a fixed patch, its sufficient rate is \(4a\epsilon+\epsilon^2\), with \(a\) a known bound on the nominal jump norm and \(\epsilon\) a supplied coefficient envelope in the known dictionary. Neither result supplies the dictionary, coefficient bounds, positive floors, geometric architecture or useful memory threshold physically.
